claim: Short-term recordings contained movement- and stimulus-related information; motor decoding used pooled bidirectional recurrent analysis.
scope: 15 rats overall; motor-decoding subset 5; 3 acute pigs.
limitation: Not a prospective chronic human decoder, expert-skill code, or demonstration of retained transfer.
design_implication: Useful causal features and chronic stability remain explicit SCCI_RH premises.
support_locator: Full publisher text and author XML; Results Figs.1, 4, 5 and Methods.

claim: Hyperflexible arrays enabled longitudinal intraspinal acquisition and wheel-running movement reconstruction.
scope: 5 mice for nine-week recording; separate movement-decoding experiment in 2 mice.
limitation: Does not validate nonpenetrating human electrodes, indefinite stable channels, or fine expert finger information.
design_implication: Recording access and durability cannot be transferred across electrode types without an assumption.
support_locator: Full publisher text and author XML; sections 2.2, 2.4.

claim: Recorded spinal events triggered stimulation across acute complete transection; experimental cortical stimulation generated test input.
scope: 16 acute rats; separate 6 passive dummy implants; human cadaver feasibility.
limitation: Passive six-week implants were not chronic active interfaces; cadaver placement was not functional human testing.
design_implication: Provides a spinal-recording-to-stimulation precedent; voluntary chronic control remains a further premise.
support_locator: Author full-text XML; Figs.5-7 and acute/cadaver Methods.

claim: In the studied setting, myelinated afferent recruitment engaged motor circuitry trans-synaptically.
scope: Rat computational field/axon models and in-vivo experiments; total cohort not independently established here.
limitation: Not universal direct motoneuron stimulation, arbitrary inhibition, or a contact-independent neural command.
design_implication: Specify a calibrated recruitment map and reachable directions.
support_locator: Author abstract via Europe PMC PMID24305828; detailed parameter tables not re-audited.

claim: Anatomy/recruitment-informed programs supported trunk and leg activities during stimulation and rehabilitation.
scope: 3 participants with complete sensorimotor paralysis.
limitation: Clinical restoration does not demonstrate healthy athletic enhancement or expert-to-novice transfer.
design_implication: Individualize anatomy, spatial recruitment and timing rather than replaying expert voltages.
support_locator: Primary abstract and author-hosted EPFL paper; study cohort stated in abstract.

claim: Immediate ON assistance and within-trial OFF changes were reported; maximum benefit required continued stimulation.
scope: 7 post-stroke participants; 4-week implant period; finger improvement in 3 with residual connectivity.
limitation: Not healthy novice acquisition, spinal-recording-based assistance, or proof that all ON benefit becomes retention.
design_implication: Score assistance, OFF retention and later follow-up separately.
support_locator: Full publisher text and author XML; abstract, assessments and Discussion.

claim: Activity-linked treatment improved reaching recovery; benefit persisted 3 stimulation-free weeks with daily retraining.
scope: 24 injured rats: 9 activity-dependent, 6 open-loop, 9 retraining-only; impairment-matched, not randomized.
limitation: Roughly doubled recovery endpoint is not a 2x healthy learning-speed multiplier or proof of the proposed STDP mechanism.
design_implication: Separate contingent practice, retained outcome, and the untested expert-information contribution.
support_locator: Full primary PMC article; Results and Materials/Methods.

claim: Conditioning modified corticospinal connection strength; timing mattered and many effects eventually reverted.
scope: 2 monkeys; 19 conditioning sessions and 15 cell/site pairs are repeated observations.
limitation: Not spinal-only recording, expert imitation, or demonstrated healthy human whole-skill transfer.
design_implication: Retain absent, reversible and adverse adaptation regimes.
support_locator: Author-hosted full manuscript and author abstract; Results and Experimental Procedures.

claim: Thirty-session H-reflex down-conditioning produced persistent reflex and locomotor changes in responders.
scope: 13 people with SCI: 9 conditioning, 4 measurement controls; 6/9 conditioned successfully.
limitation: Not invasive SCCI or direct expert-to-learner neural transfer.
design_implication: Supports plasticity and individual-response variation without relabelling peripheral access.
support_locator: Author-hosted full manuscript; Subjects, protocol and Results.

claim: Continuous stimulation could disrupt proprioceptive information; temporal/spatial strategies sought to preserve it.
scope: 3 SCI participants plus computational/preclinical experiments; some sensory tasks had smaller subsets.
limitation: Does not imply every waveform abolishes perception or determine a healthy-consumer penalty.
design_implication: Model sensory cost and assistance dependence; preserve a no-benefit case.
support_locator: Author full-text XML; human sensory/locomotor Results and Methods.

claim: The digital bridge enabled mobility; rehabilitation-related unassisted improvement was also reported.
scope: 1 participant with chronic tetraplegia; repeated home/rehabilitation observations.
limitation: Not spinal-only intent recording or proof of expert-informed healthy skill acquisition.
design_implication: Label cortical-input variants hybrid; do not credit their decoder to spinal recording.
support_locator: Author full-text XML and primary publisher PDF; abstract and Discussion.

claim: A neuroprosthetic baroreflex compensated haemodynamic deficits after SCI.
scope: Multiple rodent experiments; 3 nonhuman primates; human proof of concept in 1 participant.
limitation: Not neural BP decoding, arbitrary pressure lowering, or healthy universal autonomic automation.
design_implication: Use external physiological feedback and a target-specific positive actuator.
support_locator: Publisher abstract and accessible Extended Data 7-10; detailed main text subscription-limited.

claim: Targeted EES supported pressure regulation; waveform sampling 200 Hz, extracted measures 1 Hz, command latency as low as 25 ms are distinct.
scope: 14 implanted participants across 4 staged trials; analysis subsets differ; 1479 survey respondents are separate.
limitation: Not a spinal pressure decoder, active pressure-lowering channel, healthy enhancement, or validation of SCCI_RH hardware.
design_implication: Keep sensor freshness separate from command rate, and identify anatomy-specific pressure recruitment.
support_locator: Full publisher text and author XML; Figs.2-3 and hemodynamic/system Methods.

claim: ECAP-controlled stimulation regulated recruitment and improved the specified pain-response endpoint versus fixed output.
scope: 134 randomized chronic-pain participants, 67/arm; 125 analyzed at 3 months and 118 at 12 months.
limitation: An ECAP is not direct pain, BP or intent measurement; comparator was active open-loop stimulation, not placebo.
design_implication: Treat evoked recruitment and desired physiological state as different feedback variables.
support_locator: Primary author abstract via Europe PMC PMID31870766; full main text not re-audited.

claim: Personalized storage/voiding programs and training supported selected bladder-management outcomes.
scope: 4 consented; 3 implanted; 2 completed 12-month follow-up; 1 achieved high sustained voiding efficiency.
limitation: Not autonomous neural fullness decoding, universal emptying, or unlimited postponement; cystometry and uroflow differ.
design_implication: Broader body automation needs its own sensing, target, state transitions and failure model.
support_locator: Author full-text XML; Methods 2.4, Results 3.1-3.2 and follow-up.

claim: Combined activation approximately summed tested endpoint force fields.
scope: Spinalized frogs; animal count not independently established from accessible abstract.
limitation: Not a universal human primitive library, exact voluntary superposition, or a transferable electrode map.
design_implication: A small task-conditioned coordination space is a defensible proposal.
support_locator: Primary author abstract via Europe PMC PMID8052615.

claim: A mouse excitatory spinal neuron population was important to recovery under the studied rehabilitation paradigm.
scope: 9 humans in rehabilitation observations; separate mouse cohorts vary by experiment.
limitation: Does not locate all human expertise in one cell population or demonstrate expert-skill downloading.
design_implication: Use circuit plasticity as rationale, while leaving the specific SCCI_RH learning law assumed.
support_locator: Author full-text XML; abstract, circuit prioritization and causal perturbation Results.

claim: The public proof-of-concept repository gives an ambitious BCI concept inspectable engineering artifacts.
scope: No functional implanted human BCI validation established by reviewed repository.
limitation: Repository presence is not validation of a functioning implanted biological interface.
design_implication: Credit the engineering progression while contributing original SCCI mechanisms and designs.
support_locator: Official README/tree and commit reverified; fresh video/transcript retrieval throttled.

claim: Useful spinal task/state features arrive causally in time for a chosen intervention.
scope: Future motor mode
limitation: Published offline reconstruction does not establish this property.
design_implication: Expose observation support time, availability, uncertainty and artifact invalidity.
support_locator: docs/stage3/conditional-concept/assumption-ledger.csv

claim: A task-conditioned expert representation can be aligned to a learner-specific reachable correction map.
scope: Expert-informed motor practice
limitation: No cited experiment demonstrates this cross-person conjunction.
design_implication: Map task coordinates and separately calibrated programs; never replay expert voltage.
support_locator: docs/stage3/conditional-concept/motor-evidence.md

claim: Well-timed assistance can improve a retained component of learning beyond equal practice.
scope: Future healthy motor-learning application
limitation: Healthy acquisition and numerical learning multiplier remain unestablished.
design_implication: Declare plasticity law, OFF retention metric and adverse/zero-effect controls.
support_locator: docs/stage3/conditional-concept/motor-evidence.md

claim: Expert spinal features contain incremental useful information beyond allowed external sensors.
scope: Added value of invasive expert recording
limitation: Signal origin alone does not confer information or control advantage.
design_implication: Use equal-information and equal-resource external comparators.
support_locator: docs/stage3/information-comparison.md

claim: A selected pressure target provides stable local positive authority and timely calibrated external BP feedback.
scope: Conditional pressure-support operating episode
limitation: Zero/adverse gain, delay, saturation and existing native regulation can violate the premise.
design_implication: Bound actuation, monitor sensor quality and model withdrawal tails.
support_locator: docs/stage3/conditional-concept/physiology-evidence.md

claim: Target-specific neural recording may augment pressure-state or recruitment information.
scope: Optional pressure extension
limitation: A pressure-related spinal decoder is not established by the pressure trials.
design_implication: Keep external BP primary and test the neural contribution separately.
support_locator: docs/stage3/conditional-concept/physiology-evidence.md

claim: Motor and pressure functions need individualized lead targets and operating envelopes.
scope: Shared proposed SCCI platform
limitation: A common can or processor does not imply a universal spinal site.
design_implication: Retain modular target-specific lead concepts and separate response maps.
support_locator: docs/stage1/application-mechanisms.md

claim: Electrical delivered charge, neural recruitment and desired physiological response are distinct feedback variables.
scope: SCCI_RH acquisition/control/stimulation chain
limitation: Passing a command or electrical monitor does not prove biological benefit.
design_implication: Keep independent delivery monitoring and external functional feedback.
support_locator: docs/stage4/exit-review.md

claim: SCCI_RH includes eight native routed populated reference boards and a target-linked nRF5340 image.
scope: Digital engineering deliverable
limitation: No physical execution, analog performance or implanted qualification.
design_implication: Report linked build and CAD checks at their actual evidence level.
support_locator: provenance/stage4-integrated-pcb-verification.json

claim: The reference mechanical assembly and future can are separately inspectable native models.
scope: Stage 5 digital CAD deliverable
limitation: Compact can contains allocations; current eight boards are not miniaturized into it.
design_implication: Preserve full-scale versus future-concept distinction.
support_locator: docs/stage5/exit-review.md

claim: The common platform might extend to another specifically defined physiological function.
scope: Longer-term body-automation vision
limitation: Each function needs its own observable state, accessible authority and finite failure model.
design_implication: Do not advertise universal or indefinite bodily control.
support_locator: docs/stage1/application-mechanisms.md

claim: A bounded healthy task might show 1.5x or 2x faster acquisition.
scope: Hypothetical future target
limitation: Neither value is an SCCI_RH measurement or an effect established by the cited papers.
design_implication: Define threshold and OFF-retention interval before estimating a multiplier.
support_locator: Original hypothesis paper pp12-13
